metaDescription: Six 42-inch tow-behind lawn sweepers compared on hopper size, brush design, frame strength and upkeep, so you can match one to your tractor and yard.
expertTake: The Craftsman 42-inch with its 20 cu ft flow-through bag is the best all-round pick, and the Agri-Fab 42-inch is the value pick if your yard is small enough for a 12 cu ft bag. Anyone with a steep, wet, tree-heavy lot should skip ground-driven sweepers and look at a tractor-powered leaf vacuum instead.
introParagraphs: A tow-behind sweeper has no engine. The ground wheels spin a set of brushes through a chain or belt, and the brushes flick leaves, clippings and pine needles back into a fabric hopper that you dump from the seat.

That simplicity is the appeal, and also the limit. Pickup quality depends on ground speed, brush height, how dry the debris is and how well the hopper fills, so the spec sheet matters less than the mechanism behind it.

products.name: Craftsman 42-Inch Tow Sweeper 20 cu ft Flow-Thru Bag
products.description:
The Craftsman pairs a 42 inch brush path with a flow-through bag, where debris enters at the rear and the airflow pushes it forward so the whole 20 cu ft volume fills instead of piling up near the brush housing. That is a real mechanical advantage over a plain sack, because a bag that fills unevenly looks full long before it is.

The tradeoff is bulk. Against the 12 cu ft Agri-Fab 42-inch, you carry nearly twice the volume, which means fewer dump trips on a half-acre of oak leaves but a heavier, bulkier load for a small lawn tractor on a slope. It also handles pine cones and needles, which smaller bag-type sweepers tend to choke on.

Ownership is where this pick earns its rank. The hopper bag is the wear item, so inspect the seams every fall and store it dry. Keep the drive chain or belt tensioned, and expect to replace brush bristles after several seasons of sweeping gravel edges. It suits owners with a lawn tractor or ATV who want large capacity without moving up to a 44 or 48 inch width.
products.bestFor: Half-acre to two-acre lots with mixed leaves, needles and cones.
pros: Flow-through bag uses the full 20 cu ft volume
Picks up pine needles and cones, not just dry leaves
Universal hitch fits tractors, zero-turns and ATVs
Roomy hopper cuts dump trips on large leaf drops
cons: Bulkier to store than a 12 cu ft sweeper
Full bag adds drag on slopes for small tractors
Bag fabric needs seam checks and dry storage

products.name: Agri-Fab 42-Inch Tow Sweeper 12 cu ft Hopper
products.description:
Agri-Fab is a long-running name in ground-driven yard implements, and this 42 inch model is its straightforward entry. The brush height adjustment lets the bristles reach about 1/2 inch into the turf, which is the sweet spot for lifting clippings and fallen leaves without raking the grass root zone.

The 12 cu ft hopper is the compromise. Compared with the Craftsman at 20 cu ft or the Brinly at 20 cu ft, you stop and dump sooner, so it fits quarter-acre to half-acre yards better than big leaf-heavy properties. In return the sweeper is lighter on the hitch and easier to push around the shed by hand.

Support is the reason to buy it. Agri-Fab sells replacement parts and publishes manuals for its sweepers, which matters in year three when a bag tears or a brush wears. Cut the lawn first and sweep dry leaves, and the pull-rope dump will keep up fine. It is the sensible pick for a modest lot with a basic lawn tractor.
products.bestFor: Smaller lots and owners who want brand parts support.
pros: Brush depth adjusts to about 1/2 in into turf
Lighter load for small tractors than 20 cu ft bags
Replacement parts and manuals from a long-running brand
Pull-rope dump from the seat, no tools
cons: 12 cu ft bag fills fast in heavy leaf fall
Plain bag lacks a flow-through fill design
Not suited to very large or wet-leaf lots

products.name: YITAMOTOR 42-Inch Tow Sweeper 20 cu ft Hopper
products.description:
YITAMOTOR gives you a 20 cu ft hopper at the 42 inch width, the same volume as the Craftsman, with an adjustable sweeping height and a dump rope. The listing names leaves, weeds, twigs and grass as targets, so it is aimed at general yard cleanup instead of a single leaf season.

What you do not get is the published detail you see on the Agri-Fab, such as a stated brush penetration depth. Between the two, the Agri-Fab is the better documented machine and this is the larger-capacity option. Treat it as a capable general sweeper and verify the hitch bracket against your tow vehicle before the first pull.

Expect to do your own checks on a newer brand. Tighten every fastener after the first hour because vibration loosens bolts, and grease pivots once a season. Keep the hopper dry in storage. It makes sense when you want 20 cu ft and a rope dump and are comfortable owning a machine with thinner brand support.
products.bestFor: Yards with mixed grass, weeds and light twigs.
pros: 20 cu ft hopper matches the Craftsman volume
Handles clippings, weeds and light twigs
Hitch fits tractors, zero-turns and ATVs
Height adjustment suits changing turf
cons: Thinner brand parts support than Agri-Fab
Fasteners need a re-check after first use

products.name: MAXSA 42-Inch Tow Sweeper 21 cu ft Steel Frame
products.description:
MAXSA leads with the frame: a thick steel structure under a 21 cu ft hopper and a 42 inch sweep path. A rigid frame matters because the brush shaft sees constant shock from bumps, and a flexing frame lets the brushes drift off the ground contact line.

At 21 cu ft it is one cubic foot larger than the Craftsman and the YITAMOTOR, which is a small gap in practice. The Craftsman wins on bag design, while the MAXSA wins if you expect to tow over uneven ground and want a stiffer chassis. Neither number should be read as a performance gap by itself.

Ownership comes down to the hopper and the bristles. Rinse and dry the bag, and replace brushes when they stop touching the turf at the lowest height setting. Check the hitch pin for slop. This suits owners who value structure over bag tricks, and who mow the lawn short before sweeping.

pros: Thick steel frame holds brush alignment over bumps
21 cu ft hopper is the second largest here

products.name: Brinly 42-Inch Tow Sweeper 20 cu ft Six Brushes
products.description:
Brinly builds ground-driven lawn tools, and this sweeper uses six high-velocity brushes with an indexed height adjustment. More brush rows means more flicks per foot of travel, and the indexed settings make it repeatable, so you can return to the same height after fighting a thick patch.

Against the Agri-Fab 42-inch, which publishes a 1/2 inch penetration depth, the Brinly gives you detents but no stated depth. Its 20 cu ft hopper matches the Craftsman and YITAMOTOR, so the choice between them is brush and bag design, not capacity. Brinly is a name many tractor owners already know from its other attachments.

Upkeep is routine. Brushes wear, the bag gets stiff with debris and moisture, and the hitch needs periodic inspection. Wipe the bag dry before storage to avoid mildew. Pick it if you like the repeatable height settings and a six-brush layout over a flow-through bag.
products.bestFor: Owners who want repeatable brush height settings.
pros: Six high-velocity brushes for dense pickup
Indexed height settings are repeatable
20 cu ft hopper matches the Craftsman

cons: Plain bag fills less evenly than flow-through

products.name: VORTEXTOVE 42-Inch Tow Sweeper 24 cu ft Hopper
products.description:
VORTEXTOVE offers the biggest bag in the 42 inch group at 24 cu ft, with a lever that lifts the brush head for tool-free height changes. The broad steel brush head is meant to resist bending so sweep power stays consistent as the sweeper ages.

Capacity is the headline, but remember mechanics: at 24 cu ft against the Agri-Fab at 12 cu ft, the bag has twice the volume and needs a tow vehicle that handles the extra load when full. A bag this large can also catch wind and spill over the top on blustery days.

The lever height control makes it handy if you sweep a lawn and then a driveway or gravel path with the same unit. Keep the brush from digging into gravel, since stones wear bristles quickly. Choose it if your priority is the fewest stops on a leaf-heavy property and you have the pulling power.
products.bestFor: Leaf-heavy lots where fewer dump trips matter most.
pros: 24 cu ft is the largest hopper in this group

Works on lawn, pavement and gravel

buyingCriteria.explanation: Hopper size is quoted in cubic feet, but the weight of a full bag depends on moisture. A 12 cu ft bag like the Agri-Fab 42-inch suits a small lawn tractor, while the 24 cu ft VORTEXTOVE or the 21 cu ft MAXSA asks more of the drawbar. The common mistake is buying the largest bag, then finding it stalls on hills when loaded with damp leaves.

Brushes spin because the ground wheels turn them, so pickup depends on how fast you drive. Slow tractor speed means slow brushes and leaves left behind. Agri-Fab cites a 5.6 to 1 brush-to-wheel ratio on its 44-inch model, a reminder that this spec exists, yet few listings in this group publish one. Ask for it, and drive at a brisk walk to light jog pace.

A flow-through bag like the Craftsman 20 cu ft one lets air exit through the bag as debris enters, so the volume fills from back to front. A plain bag packs near the opening and reports full early. The extra fill efficiency is real, but only if you sweep dry leaves; wet matted leaves stick to any bag.

The brushes should just touch the grass tips. The Agri-Fab reaches about 1/2 inch into turf, and the Brinly offers indexed settings. Too low drags bristles, wears them quickly and loads the tow vehicle. Too high leaves leaves behind. Lever systems like the VORTEXTOVE are quick to change, which matters when you cross from lawn to driveway.

The brush shaft takes shock from every bump, so a thin frame will flex and let brushes lose contact. The MAXSA lists a thick steel frame, which is the right feature for uneven ground. Check the hitch pin and bracket on any model before towing, since a loose hitch fails on the first sharp turn.

The bag and the bristles are the parts that fail, usually by year three. Agri-Fab and Brinly are established attachment names, so a replacement bag is easier to find than for newer brands. Before buying, search for the bag by model number; if you cannot find one, plan on sewing or replacing the whole unit.

specDecoder.meaning: This is the brush path, not the overall width of the machine. A 42 inch sweeper is wider than that on the frame, so the wheels run outside the swept strip.
specDecoder.watchFor: Measure gates and lane widths against the frame, not just the 42 inch figure, on every sweeper in this lineup.

specDecoder.meaning: Volume of the bag when fully inflated, not how much debris it holds in real use. Wet leaves and compaction cut usable volume sharply.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 12 cu ft Agri-Fab bag and a 24 cu ft VORTEXTOVE bag differ by a factor of two, but the large bag only matters if your tractor can pull it full.

specDecoder.meaning: How many brush turns you get per wheel turn. Higher ratios spin the brushes faster at the same ground speed.
specDecoder.watchFor: Most listings here omit this number, so compare brush count and diameter instead, such as the Brinly's six brushes.

specDecoder.meaning: Debris enters at the back and the air exits through the fabric, filling the bag evenly front to back.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Craftsman lists this design among the picks; the rest use a simple sack.

specDecoder.meaning: How far bristles reach into the grass blade zone. About 1/2 inch lifts clippings without digging.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Agri-Fab states this value; for the others, test height settings on a small patch first.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mechanism fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each sweeper moves debris, from brush count to bag design. The Craftsman flow-through bag and the Brinly six-brush layout were weighed against plain sacks. A machine that fills its bag efficiently scored higher than one with the same volume on paper.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity versus towing load
howWeEvaluated.description: We read hopper sizes from 12 cu ft on the Agri-Fab up to 24 cu ft on the VORTEXTOVE and matched each to the tow vehicle that can pull it full. Bigger was not automatically better. Overloading a small tractor on a slope is a real failure mode.

howWeEvaluated.title: Frame and hitch construction
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet, we looked for steel frame, hitch type and adjustment hardware. The MAXSA steel frame and universal hitches stood out. Machines without a described structure scored lower on durability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated common owner complaints about bag tears, short dump ropes and loosening fasteners. These issues recur across the category, so we favored models with accessible parts support.

howWeEvaluated.title: Parts and brand support
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed how easy it is to find a replacement bag or brush. Established names like Agri-Fab and Brinly ranked above newer listings with no parts history.

cards.label: Flow-through bag
cards.text: Air passes through the fabric so debris fills from the back to the front and uses the whole volume. The Craftsman 42-inch is the one in this lineup built this way.

cards.label: Plain bag
cards.text: Debris packs near the opening and the bag looks full early. The Agri-Fab, YITAMOTOR, MAXSA, Brinly and VORTEXTOVE use this layout, which is fine on a small lot.

howToChoose.note: Pick the Craftsman for big leaf loads, a plain-bag model for small tidy lots.

rows: Indexed settings return to the same height
Lever lifts the brush head, no tools
Set and forget on steady ground

howToChoose.subheading: For Pine Needles and Cones Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A high-volume bag that fills evenly and brushes that engage low enough to catch needles. Heavy cones need a stiff brush head and a sturdy bag seam.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Craftsman 42-inch lists pine needles and cones as targets and has the flow-through bag, so it is the clear choice. The MAXSA is the fallback if you need a stiffer frame.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have over half an acre, uneven ground or heavy leaf fall. The Craftsman 42-inch with 20 cu ft or the MAXSA 42-inch with its steel frame earn their extra cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small, flat, tidy lawn. The Agri-Fab 42-inch at 12 cu ft is plenty, and a larger bag only adds weight.

maintenance.task: Inspect and dry the hopper bag
maintenance.why: Moist debris causes mildew and weakens the fabric. Seams are where tears start, so check them before every season.
Worn bristles stop touching the turf at the lowest height setting. Replace brushes before pickup quality drops.

maintenance.interval: First hour, then monthly in use
maintenance.why: Vibration loosens bolts. A loose hitch pin can drop the sweeper on a sharp turn.
Dry pivots bind the height lever. A dry drive chain wears faster.
The wheels drive the brushes. A flat or worn wheel slows the brushes and cuts pickup.

faq.q: Is a 42 inch sweeper big enough for my yard?
faq.a: A 42 inch path suits most lots up to about an acre when pulled by a lawn tractor. Larger properties benefit from a 44 or 48 inch width to cut passes.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a 42 inch sweeper?
faq.a: The spread between the Agri-Fab 42-inch and the Craftsman 42-inch is modest in relative terms. Spend more only if you need a bigger bag or a stiffer frame.

faq.q: How long will a tow sweeper last?
faq.a: The frame outlasts the bag and bristles. Expect to replace the hopper bag and brushes by year three with regular use, and store the unit dry.

faq.q: Does a bigger hopper mean better pickup?
faq.a: No. Pickup depends on brush speed and height. A 24 cu ft VORTEXTOVE bag only reduces dump trips, it does not improve sweeping.
Poorly. Wet leaves mat and clog any bag. Wait for dry conditions or mow first to chop them.

faq.q: What does a lawn sweeper not replace?
faq.a: It does not shred or handle thick heavy brush. Check the owner's manual for tow vehicle weight limits and keep passersby clear while towing.
